result.markdown: --- title: "Pronóstico horario de bicicletas en Seúl" subtitle: "Un caso autocontenido con tidyverse y tidymodels" author: "Miguelangel Palma Rojas" date: last-modified lang: es description: "Código visible de principio a fin para pronosticar demanda, evaluado sobre un holdout estrictamente futuro." --- La demanda horaria no es solamente un problema predictivo. Es una decisión operativa: cuántas bicicletas deben estar disponibles, dónde habrá presión y cuánta incertidumbre persiste durante las horas pico. Este notebook es autocontenido de forma intencional. Cada transformación, partición, modelo, métrica y gráfico utilizado está escrito aquí y se ejecuta en orden. ## Paquetes y reproducibilidad ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(ranger) library(knitr) tidymodels_prefer() set.seed(2026) ``` ::: ## Contrato y calidad de datos El snapshot gobernado contiene una fila por fecha y hora. Antes de modelar, el notebook comprueba el esquema completo, datos faltantes, rangos físicos, alquileres no negativos y llaves fecha-hora únicas. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} required_columns <- c( "date", "rented_bike_count", "hour", "temperature_c", "humidity_pct", "wind_speed_ms", "visibility_10m", "dew_point_c", "solar_radiation_mj_m2", "rainfall_mm", "snowfall_cm", "season", "holiday", "functioning_day", "weekday", "is_weekend" ) bikes <- read_csv( "data/seoul_bike_snapshot.csv", show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(date = col_date()) ) |> mutate( weekday = factor( weekday, levels = c( "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday" ) ), across(c(season, holiday, functioning_day, is_weekend), factor) ) |> arrange(date, hour) stopifnot( setequal(names(bikes), required_columns), !anyNA(bikes), all(bikes$rented_bike_count >= 0), all(bikes$hour %in% 0:23), between(min(bikes$humidity_pct), 0, 100), between(max(bikes$humidity_pct), 0, 100), nrow(distinct(bikes, date, hour)) == nrow(bikes) ) data_profile <- bikes |> summarise( observations = n(), first_date = min(date), last_date = max(date), operating_days = n_distinct(date[functioning_day == "Yes"]), closure_hours = sum(functioning_day == "No"), average_hourly_demand = mean(rented_bike_count), peak_hourly_demand = max(rented_bike_count), missing_cells = sum(is.na(pick(everything()))) ) data_profile |> kable(digits = 1, caption = "Perfil validado del snapshot") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Perfil validado del snapshot | observations|first_date |last_date | operating_days| closure_hours| average_hourly_demand| peak_hourly_demand| missing_cells| |------------:|:----------|:----------|--------------:|-------------:|---------------------:|------------------:|-------------:| | 8760|2017-12-01 |2018-11-30 | 353| 295| 704.6| 3556| 0| ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bikes |> filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |> summarise( average_demand = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = c(weekday, hour) ) |> ggplot(aes(hour, weekday, fill = average_demand)) + geom_tile() + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) + labs( title = "Los picos de viaje definen el ritmo operativo", x = "Hora", y = "Día", fill = "Alquileres promedio" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Alquileres promedio por día y hora durante días operativos.](index_files/figure-html/ritmo-demanda-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Variables y holdout futuro Los cierres se manejan como una regla de servicio, no como demanda cero aprendida. El 20% final de las fechas completas se reserva intacto para la evaluación definitiva. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} origin_date <- min(bikes$date) model_data <- bikes |> filter(functioning_day == "Yes") |> transmute( date, rented_bike_count, hour = factor(hour, levels = 0:23), weekday, month = factor(format(date, "%m"), levels = sprintf("%02d", 1:12)), season, holiday, is_weekend, trend_day = as.numeric(date - origin_date), temperature_c, humidity_pct, wind_speed_ms, visibility_10m, dew_point_c, solar_radiation_mj_m2, rainfall_mm, snowfall_cm ) |> arrange(date, hour) test_days <- ceiling(n_distinct(model_data$date) * 0.20) first_test_date <- model_data |> distinct(date) |> arrange(desc(date)) |> slice_head(n = test_days) |> summarise(first_test_date = min(date)) |> pull(first_test_date) training_data <- model_data |> filter(date < first_test_date) testing_data <- model_data |> filter(date >= first_test_date) tibble( muestra = c("Entrenamiento", "Holdout futuro"), primera_fecha = c(min(training_data$date), min(testing_data$date)), ultima_fecha = c(max(training_data$date), max(testing_data$date)), observaciones = c(nrow(training_data), nrow(testing_data)) ) |> kable(caption = "Partición cronológica final") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Particin cronolgica final |muestra |primera_fecha |ultima_fecha | observaciones| |:--------------|:-------------|:------------|-------------:| |Entrenamiento |2017-12-01 |2018-09-10 | 6768| |Holdout futuro |2018-09-11 |2018-11-30 | 1697| ::: ::: ## Validación temporal expansiva Los hiperparámetros se seleccionan únicamente dentro del entrenamiento. Cada ventana de validación de 28 días ocurre después de un entrenamiento expansivo y una separación de un día. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} training_dates <- training_data |> distinct(date) |> arrange(date) |> pull(date) assessment_days <- 28L gap_days <- 1L analysis_ends <- round(seq( floor(length(training_dates) * 0.45), length(training_dates) - assessment_days - gap_days, length.out = 4 )) |> as.integer() assessment_starts <- analysis_ends + gap_days + 1L assessment_ends <- assessment_starts + assessment_days - 1L split_01 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[1]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[1]]:assessment_ends[[1]]]) ), training_data ) split_02 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[2]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[2]]:assessment_ends[[2]]]) ), training_data ) split_03 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[3]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[3]]:assessment_ends[[3]]]) ), training_data ) split_04 <- make_splits( list( analysis = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[seq_len(analysis_ends[[4]])]), assessment = which(training_data$date %in% training_dates[assessment_starts[[4]]:assessment_ends[[4]]]) ), training_data ) temporal_splits <- list(split_01, split_02, split_03, split_04) temporal_resamples <- manual_rset( temporal_splits, paste0("Ventana", str_pad(seq_along(temporal_splits), 2, pad = "0")) ) window_summary <- tibble( ventana = temporal_resamples$id, inicio_entrenamiento = c( min(analysis(split_01)$date), min(analysis(split_02)$date), min(analysis(split_03)$date), min(analysis(split_04)$date) ), fin_entrenamiento = c( max(analysis(split_01)$date), max(analysis(split_02)$date), max(analysis(split_03)$date), max(analysis(split_04)$date) ), inicio_validacion = c( min(assessment(split_01)$date), min(assessment(split_02)$date), min(assessment(split_03)$date), min(assessment(split_04)$date) ), fin_validacion = c( max(assessment(split_01)$date), max(assessment(split_02)$date), max(assessment(split_03)$date), max(assessment(split_04)$date) ), filas_entrenamiento = c( nrow(analysis(split_01)), nrow(analysis(split_02)), nrow(analysis(split_03)), nrow(analysis(split_04)) ), filas_validacion = c( nrow(assessment(split_01)), nrow(assessment(split_02)), nrow(assessment(split_03)), nrow(assessment(split_04)) ) ) window_summary |> kable(caption = "Ventanas expansivas de validación") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Ventanas expansivas de validacin |ventana |inicio_entrenamiento |fin_entrenamiento |inicio_validacion |fin_validacion | filas_entrenamiento| filas_validacion| |:---------|:--------------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:--------------|-------------------:|----------------:| |Ventana01 |2017-12-01 |2018-04-05 |2018-04-07 |2018-05-05 | 3024| 672| |Ventana02 |2017-12-01 |2018-05-19 |2018-05-21 |2018-06-17 | 4032| 672| |Ventana03 |2017-12-01 |2018-07-01 |2018-07-03 |2018-07-30 | 5064| 672| |Ventana04 |2017-12-01 |2018-08-12 |2018-08-14 |2018-09-10 | 6072| 672| ::: ::: ## Preprocesamiento y especificaciones La receta identifica la fecha, codifica las señales categóricas, elimina columnas sin varianza o linealmente dependientes y normaliza los predictores numéricos. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bike_recipe <- recipe(rented_bike_count ~ ., data = training_data) |> update_role(date, new_role = "id") |> step_unknown(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |> step_zv(all_predictors()) |> step_lincomb(all_numeric_predictors()) |> step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) linear_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model(linear_reg() |> set_engine("lm")) elastic_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model( linear_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = tune()) |> set_engine("glmnet") ) forest_workflow <- workflow() |> add_recipe(bike_recipe) |> add_model( rand_forest(mtry = tune(), min_n = tune(), trees = 300) |> set_engine( "ranger", importance = "permutation", num.threads = 1, seed = 2029 ) |> set_mode("regression") ) ``` ::: Aquí se muestra únicamente el código fuente. La impresión interna y extensa de la receta y del workflow se oculta porque no aporta valor analítico. ## Ajuste y modelos finales ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tuning_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, mae) set.seed(2027) elastic_grid <- grid_space_filling( penalty(range = c(-5, 0)), mixture(), size = 6 ) elastic_tuning <- tune_grid( elastic_workflow, resamples = temporal_resamples, grid = elastic_grid, metrics = tuning_metrics, control = control_grid(allow_par = FALSE) ) best_elastic <- select_best(elastic_tuning, metric = "rmse") set.seed(2028) forest_grid <- grid_space_filling( mtry(range = c(4L, 18L)), min_n(range = c(5L, 40L)), size = 6 ) forest_tuning <- tune_grid( forest_workflow, resamples = temporal_resamples, grid = forest_grid, metrics = tuning_metrics, control = control_grid(allow_par = FALSE) ) best_forest <- select_best(forest_tuning, metric = "rmse") linear_fit <- fit(linear_workflow, training_data) elastic_fit <- elastic_workflow |> finalize_workflow(best_elastic) |> fit(training_data) set.seed(2029) forest_fit <- forest_workflow |> finalize_workflow(best_forest) |> fit(training_data) ``` ::: ## Resultados finales El baseline promedia la demanda histórica por día y hora. Si no existe una combinación, usa el promedio por hora y luego el promedio global del entrenamiento. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} calendar_average <- training_data |> summarise(calendar_average = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = c(hour, weekday)) hourly_average <- training_data |> summarise(hour_average = mean(rented_bike_count), .by = hour) calendar_predictions <- testing_data |> left_join(calendar_average, by = c("hour", "weekday")) |> left_join(hourly_average, by = "hour") |> transmute( date, hour, rented_bike_count, .pred = coalesce( calendar_average, hour_average, mean(training_data$rented_bike_count) ), model = "Baseline de calendario" ) linear_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(linear_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Regresión lineal") elastic_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(elastic_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Elastic Net") forest_predictions <- testing_data |> select(date, hour, rented_bike_count) |> bind_cols(predict(forest_fit, new_data = testing_data)) |> mutate(.pred = pmax(0, .pred), model = "Random forest") predictions <- bind_rows( calendar_predictions, linear_predictions, elastic_predictions, forest_predictions ) peak_threshold <- quantile( training_data$rented_bike_count, probs = 0.90, names = FALSE ) model_metrics <- predictions |> summarise( rmse = sqrt(mean((rented_bike_count - .pred)^2)), mae = mean(abs(rented_bike_count - .pred)), rsq = rsq_trad_vec(rented_bike_count, .pred), wape_pct = 100 * sum(abs(rented_bike_count - .pred)) / sum(rented_bike_count), sesgo = mean(.pred - rented_bike_count), mae_pico = mean( abs(rented_bike_count[rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold] - .pred[rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold]) ), .by = model ) |> arrange(rmse) leader <- model_metrics |> slice_min(rmse, n = 1) baseline_rmse <- model_metrics |> filter(model == "Baseline de calendario") |> pull(rmse) improvement <- 100 * (baseline_rmse - leader$rmse) / baseline_rmse model_metrics |> mutate( rmse = round(rmse, 1), mae = round(mae, 1), rsq = round(rsq, 1), wape_pct = round(wape_pct, 1), sesgo = round(sesgo, 1), mae_pico = round(mae_pico, 1) ) |> kable(caption = "Métricas operativas sobre fechas futuras no vistas") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Mtricas operativas sobre fechas futuras no vistas |model | rmse| mae| rsq| wape_pct| sesgo| mae_pico| |:-----------------------|-----:|-----:|---:|--------:|------:|--------:| |Random forest | 319.6| 225.9| 0.7| 25.2| -55.5| 564.0| |Elastic Net | 365.1| 268.6| 0.6| 30.0| -77.7| 713.6| |Regresin lineal | 414.0| 321.5| 0.5| 35.9| -204.1| 784.5| |Baseline de calendario | 444.0| 323.7| 0.5| 36.2| -206.5| 866.4| ::: ::: ::: {.metric-grid} ::: {.metric-card} Random forest Mejor modelo final ::: ::: {.metric-card} 319.6 bicicletas RMSE en holdout ::: ::: {.metric-card} 28.0% Mejora frente al baseline ::: ::: {.metric-card} 564 bicicletas MAE en demanda pico ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Decisión principal El modelo ganador sirve como señal de planeación, no como regla autónoma de despacho. Mejora la referencia de calendario, pero su sesgo negativo y mayor error en picos exigen un margen operativo de seguridad. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_metrics |> ggplot(aes(rmse, reorder(model, -rmse), fill = model)) + geom_col(show.legend = FALSE, width = 0.68) + geom_text(aes(label = round(rmse, 1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) + scale_fill_viridis_d(end = 0.85) + labs(title = "Error final por modelo", x = "RMSE (bicicletas)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Un RMSE menor es mejor; la evaluación usa únicamente el holdout futuro.](index_files/figure-html/comparacion-modelos-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Diagnóstico operativo ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} winning_model <- leader$model[[1]] predictions |> filter(model == winning_model, date >= max(date) - 6) |> mutate(timestamp = as.POSIXct(date) + as.numeric(as.character(hour)) * 3600) |> select(timestamp, observado = rented_bike_count, predicho = .pred) |> pivot_longer(c(observado, predicho), names_to = "serie", values_to = "bicicletas") |> ggplot(aes(timestamp, bicicletas, color = serie)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.75) + scale_color_manual(values = c(observado = "#264653", predicho = "#E76F51")) + labs( title = str_c("Demanda observada y predicha — ", winning_model), x = NULL, y = "Bicicletas", color = NULL ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Demanda observada y modelo ganador durante los últimos siete días.](index_files/figure-html/serie-holdout-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} predictions |> filter(model == winning_model) |> mutate( hour = as.integer(as.character(hour)), residual = rented_bike_count - .pred, peak = rented_bike_count >= peak_threshold ) |> ggplot(aes(hour, residual, color = peak)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#6C757D") + geom_jitter(width = 0.18, alpha = 0.25) + geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "#E76F51") + scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#457B9D", `TRUE` = "#D62828")) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 23, 3)) + labs( title = "Los errores en horas pico siguen siendo el mayor reto", x = "Hora", y = "Observado menos predicho", color = "Demanda pico" ) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Los residuales positivos representan subestimación.](index_files/figure-html/errores-pico-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} variable_importance <- forest_fit |> extract_fit_engine() |> pluck("variable.importance") |> enframe(name = "variable", value = "importance") |> arrange(desc(importance)) |> slice_head(n = 12) variable_importance |> ggplot(aes(importance, reorder(variable, importance))) + geom_col(fill = "#2A9D8F") + labs(title = "Importancia por permutación", x = "Importancia", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![La importancia por permutación describe aporte predictivo, no causalidad.](index_files/figure-html/importancia-variables-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: Temperatura, tendencia, humedad, radiación solar e indicadores de hora pico concentran buena parte de la señal. Son entradas útiles para pronosticar, no palancas causales. ## Del pronóstico a la acción - Actualizar el pronóstico antes de cada turno con el clima esperado más reciente. - Traducir alquileres esperados a metas por estación únicamente al incorporar inventario y flujos de viaje. - Añadir un margen pico cuando el costo de quedarse sin bicicletas supere el costo de capacidad ociosa. - Monitorear WAPE, sesgo y MAE pico por temporada; reentrenar cuando excedan umbrales acordados. - Tratar cierres con una regla explícita de servicio, fuera del modelo de demanda. Los datos cubren un año y no incluyen estación, capacidad, precios, eventos ni clima pronosticado. El caso demuestra una evaluación sólida, pero todavía no constituye un sistema de rebalanceo productivo. Consulta la [metodología](../docs/methodology.md), [ficha del modelo](../docs/model-card.md) y [diccionario de datos](../docs/data-dictionary.md).
